about.title: IT-news — articles on development, economics and science
about.lead: A publication for people who write code and want to understand what is going on around it: technology deep dives, plain explanations, and material that is still useful a week later.

it.name: Development
it.text: Frontend and backend, tools and approaches: React and Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, state managers, Go, Rust, Python. Walkthroughs with real code, not a retelling of the docs.

economics.name: Economics
economics.text: How the money around technology works: product unit economics, inflation and rates, investing, cryptocurrencies and how to store them.

science.name: Science
science.text: Big topics in plain language: the James Webb telescope, CRISPR genome editing, quantum computing, black holes.

articleOfTheDay.name: Article of the day
articleOfTheDay.text: The most-read piece is pulled onto the home page — a good place to start when you are not sure what to read.

snippetOfTheDay.name: Snippet of the day
snippetOfTheDay.text: A different code snippet from our articles every day, copied to the clipboard in one click.

filters.name: Search and filters
filters.text: Search by title, sort by date, views or name, filter by topic, and switch between two list layouts.

ratings.name: Article ratings
ratings.text: Leave a rating and feedback so authors can tell which pieces actually landed.

comments.name: Comments
comments.text: A discussion under every article: questions for the author, clarifications and other people's experience.

themes.name: Light and dark themes
themes.text: One click to switch, remembered between visits — comfortable to read at any time of day.

about.stackText: The project runs on React 18 and TypeScript, organised with Feature-Sliced Design. State is handled by Redux Toolkit and RTK Query, bundling by Webpack 5, testing by Jest, Testing Library and Playwright. It is a production-style learning project: the UI, the architecture and the tests are all real.
about.ctaText: Over 30 pieces on development, economics and science — with real code and no filler.
